acceptanceCriteria: ticket create and ticket refine accept a semantically valid payload with whitespace, unsorted object keys and unsorted set arrays, and record the same mutation digest as the canonical form, with a regression test per case; or every non-canonical refusal names the exact fix (whitespace, key order, the unsorted array path), with a test per case
Pretty-printed JSON never reports 'expected object key' when the only defect is whitespace
body: Filed 2026-10-04 under V1-0720 item 1 (memory corvint-tasks-payload-canonical). Observed on corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.202 against a scratch store seeded from this repo's queue.json and policy.json, with a ticket create payload that is otherwise valid: (a) json.dumps(indent=1) with newlines folded to spaces refuses 'MALFORMED: byte 1: expected object key', which names neither whitespace nor canonical form; (b) default json.dumps separators refuse 'byte 22: insignificant whitespace is not canonical'; (c) keys in reverse order refuse 'byte 2: non-canonical encoding (key order, whitespace or escape form)'; (d) unsorted labels refuse '/payload/labels: array is not canonical-byte sorted at index 1'. Every agent rebuilds the same json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) plus sorted() recipe, and a saved memory exists only to carry it. Expected: the CLI parses any valid JSON payload for the closed schema and canonicalizes it (sorted keys, compact separators, literal UTF-8, sorted set arrays, never sorting ordered arrays such as argv) before the receipt digest, or, if canonical input must stay a wire rule, every refusal names the exact transformation. Related: V1-0329 (payload errors do not lead to a valid payload in one step).
title: corvint-tasks: non-canonical payloads are refused instead of canonicalized, and pretty-printed JSON reports a misleading byte-1 error
